explanation: Modern C++ introduces smart pointers as a safer and more expressive alternative to raw pointers for resource management. They automate memory management through RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization), ensuring proper deallocation and preventing common issues like memory leaks and dangling pointers. Smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr, and std::weak_ptr enable clear ownership semantics and facilitate exception-safe code, making resource management explicit and less error-prone in C++ programming.
